YOURSELF
Ada Cole
Close

Rested, steady and ready for a real day.

Your body. 5 ft 1 in and 182 lb, with a body mass index of 34.1, in the obese range. In feet, inches and pounds, the units of the United States, where you live.

Mending. A sprained ankle, until September 19, 2026.

On your papers. Pronouns they/them. A citizen of the United States.

Energy
94/100. What’s left in you for today. Sleep brings it back.
Stress
6/100. How wound up you are. High stress spoils your sleep.
Sleep Debt
1 hour. Sleep you owe, which a night pays back.
Morale
86/100. Your mood. When it’s up, a night clears more of the day’s stress.
Condition
99/100. How sound your body is. It sets how much energy a night gives back, where your morale settles, when a sick day is excused, and how likely a year is to be your last.
Fitness
47/100. How trained your body is: the Stamina on your Player Profile. It sets how far rest can mend your condition and how much energy a workout costs.
Nourishment
59/100. How well fed you are. A meal puts it back.
Hygiene
79/100. How clean you are. When it’s low, it drags on your morale, and on readiness a little.
Readiness
How ready you are today, from all of these but fitness. It sets what a class, a lab, a rehearsal, an hour of practice or a workout builds, and how well your work goes when it’s judged.
An Injury
What it is, when it mends, and what it keeps you from.
Your Own Plans
Everything you’ve put on the calendar yourself.

Your wellbeing: eight measures that move with the hours you keep, the work you do, what you can afford and the kind of person you are. Home shows Energy and Stress, and all eight are here.

Ada Cole
YOUR WELLBEING
Energy
Close

94. Plenty for a full day.

Energy is what you have left for today. It runs down every hour you’re awake, faster when you owe sleep. Only sleep brings it back: a meal doesn’t. Your stamina is something else: how long you can keep going in a long scene or a night on stage. So is your condition: how sound your body is.

From 0 to 100. It changes with every hour the clock runs.

Ada Cole
YOUR WELLBEING
Stress
Close

6. Not much is adding to it. Running out of energy would, and so would money trouble or bad nights.

Stress is how wound up you are. It eases while you have energy left and climbs once you run out, and money you owe adds to it every day. Over 75, it wears your condition down every hour.

From 0 to 100. It changes with every hour the clock runs.

Ada Cole
YOUR WELLBEING
Sleep Debt
Close

None to speak of. You’re caught up on sleep.

Sleep debt is the sleep you owe. Every waking hour adds a little, and a night’s sleep pays it back. The more you owe, the faster your energy runs down and the less a night gives back.

Counted in hours. Each waking hour adds about a third of an hour, and a night pays it back, a long night faster. A night under six hours adds some too, and the shortest add more than they pay back.

Ada Cole
YOUR WELLBEING
Morale
Close

86. In good spirits. Each night moves it toward 85. Above 62, a night clears more of the day’s stress than usual.

Morale is your mood. Meals, workouts, unwinding and good nights lift it. Hunger, grime, money trouble and an injury pull it down.

From 0 to 100. It changes with every hour the clock runs.

Ada Cole
YOUR WELLBEING
Condition
Close

99. As sound as rest can make you at your fitness. Above 98, it settles back toward 98 each midnight. The lower it is, the likelier a year is to be your last.

Condition is how sound your body is. Illness, hunger, stress and short nights wear it down, and a good night’s rest mends it, as far as your fitness allows. Energy is about today, and condition changes more slowly. Your health is something else again: a long-term condition such as asthma, your health cover and your medical care are on Papers, under Health Cover.

From 0 to 100. It changes with every hour the clock runs.

Ada Cole
YOUR WELLBEING
Fitness
Close

47. At this fitness, rest can mend your condition to 98, and a workout costs 10 energy. At 24, training can take it to 99 at most. The body is near its best, and age takes very little from it.

Fitness is how trained your body is, and it’s the same figure as Stamina on your Player Profile: how long you can keep going in a long scene or a night on stage before you tire. Working out builds it. It holds for 3 days after a workout, then slowly falls. Rest doesn’t build it: rest brings back energy and condition.

From 0 to 100. It changes with every hour the clock runs.

Ada Cole
YOUR WELLBEING
Nourishment
Close

59. Getting hungry. Under 20, hunger costs condition and morale every hour. Each morning the day’s groceries bring it up to at least 76, or only to 40 on a day there’s no money for food.

Nourishment is how well fed you are. It falls every hour you’re awake, and a meal puts it back.

From 0 to 100. It changes with every hour the clock runs.

Ada Cole
YOUR WELLBEING
Hygiene
Close

79. Clean enough not to bother you. The morning shower brings it up to at least 82.

Hygiene is how clean you are. It falls through the day, and a shower puts it back.

From 0 to 100. It changes with every hour the clock runs.

Ada Cole
HOW READY YOU ARE TODAY
Readiness
Close

95. Nourishment is holding you back most.

Nourishment
At 59, and pulling readiness down.

Seven of the eight measures, all but fitness, from 5 to 100. It sets how much a class, a lab, a rehearsal, an hour of practice or a workout builds, and under 60 it costs you in judged work.

Ada Cole
AN INJURY
A Sprained Ankle
Close

It mends by September 19, 2026. Until then you can’t work out, and it holds back the physical side of your work. Call In Sick, on School, excuses a day of classes while it mends.

Condition
How sound your body is. An injury doesn’t lower it, but it adds to your stress and lowers your morale each day.

How long it takes depends on the injury and on how resilient the body is.
